title: The Town That Couldn't Stop Dancing | The Dancing Plague of 1518
description:
In the summer of 1518, a woman in Strasbourg began to dance in the street — and within weeks, hundreds had joined her, unable to stop. It really happened, and historians still can't fully explain it.

Sources: contemporary Strasbourg chronicles and physician records; modern analyses by historian John Waller and others. Details such as the death toll are debated.

scenes.narration: In July of 1518, in the city of Strasbourg, a woman stepped into the street and began to dance. There was no music, no festival, no reason. And for days, she did not stop.
scenes.image_prompt: a lone woman dancing in an empty cobblestone street of a medieval European town in summer, timber-framed houses, confused onlookers in doorways, warm afternoon light
scenes.sfx: distant town murmur, a lone footstep rhythm, quiet unease

scenes.narration: Her name is often recorded as Frau Troffea. Neighbors watched, amused at first, then uneasy. She danced into the night and through the next day, her feet bruised and bleeding, yet she could not seem to make herself stop.
highlight: she could not make herself stop
scenes.image_prompt: an exhausted medieval woman still dancing at dusk in a town square, worried townsfolk gathering and whispering, long shadows, dramatic golden light
scenes.sfx: soft worried whispers, evening birds, a faint uneasy drone

scenes.narration: Then something impossible happened. Within a week, more than thirty people had joined her. Within a month, by some accounts, as many as four hundred were dancing through the streets of Strasbourg.
scenes.image_prompt: a crowd of medieval townspeople dancing wildly through narrow city streets, a sea of swirling figures, chaotic and surreal, dramatic overcast light
scenes.sfx: a swelling crowd, shuffling feet, mounting commotion

scenes.narration: The city's physicians were baffled. They decided the cause was 'hot blood' — and that the only cure was to let the afflicted dance it out of their bodies.
scenes.image_prompt: medieval physicians in long robes examining exhausted dancers, consulting in a stone hall, candlelight and worried faces, historical detail
scenes.sfx: low serious voices, echoing stone hall, a ticking tension

scenes.narration: So the authorities made a staggering decision. They cleared guild halls, built a wooden stage, and even hired musicians and dancers to keep the afflicted moving. It only made things far, far worse.
scenes.image_prompt: a wooden stage erected in a medieval square with hired musicians playing while crowds dance, torches, a chaotic festival turned nightmare, dramatic dusk
scenes.sfx: fifes and drums playing, a crowd roaring, overwhelming energy

scenes.narration: People danced until they dropped from exhaustion. Contemporary accounts claim some collapsed and did not rise again — though how many truly died is still debated by historians today.
scenes.image_prompt: weary dancers slumping to the ground at the edge of a medieval square at night while others still move, somber torchlight, tasteful and atmospheric, no gore
scenes.sfx: fading music, heavy breathing, a mournful wind

scenes.narration: By September, the dancing faded as mysteriously as it had begun. Was it poisoning from moldy grain? Mass panic in a time of famine and fear? Even now, five centuries later, no one is truly certain. The town simply… stopped dancing.
scenes.image_prompt: a quiet empty medieval town square at misty dawn, scattered abandoned shoes on the cobblestones, soft hopeful morning light, stillness after chaos
scenes.sfx: gentle dawn wind, a single distant church bell, calm
